text:
maria: heads up — customer reported duplicate successful creates after a 429. they used the js sdk default config. any idea what the sdk retries by default?
raj: can you paste the request/response snippets? esp headers (Retry-After) and whether they set an idempotency key
maria: here is the minimal repro they shared:
```
POST /v1/resources
Content-Type: application/json
# no Idempotency-Key header
Body: {"name": "test"}

<- 429 Too Many Requests
   Retry-After: 3

client retried after 3s and got 200
client retried again later and got 200 (two resources created)
```
ben: quick summary from SDK side: js-sdk@1.x has these defaults — 4 retries on network errors/5xx, and it will retry on 429 if either Retry-After is present or the retry budget allows. there is jitter+expo backoff. that means without Idempotency-Key a retried POST can create duplicates.
emily: yep — we saw this pattern before. non-idempotent POSTs + retries + intermittent 429 => duplicate creates/billing. customers assume 429 is temporary and sdk will buffer/retry, but that only avoids errors, doesn't guarantee exactly-once.
raj: do we have a recommended short-term doc blurb we can send to the customer? also want reproducible steps to show it's client-side.
ben: suggested reply (short): "The SDK will retry transient 5xx/429s by default — to avoid duplicates for mutating ops, send an Idempotency-Key header or switch to client-side dedupe. If you cannot set idempotency, reduce retries in the SDK or handle 429 explicitly."
maria: adding a config snippet the customer can apply: 
```js
// reduce retries + enable idempotency header example
const client = new Redwood({
  retry: { maxRetries: 1, backoff: 'exponential', jitter: true },
  defaultHeaders: { 'Idempotency-Key': generateUuid() }
});
```
raj: for repro steps I asked them to: 1) remove Idempotency-Key 2) send rapid POSTs until we hit rate limit 3) watch server logs for duplicate creates vs attempt IDs.
emily: also note — some older SDK builds ignore Retry-After and fall back to a fixed delay; ask the customer to report sdk version.
sdk-bot: [sdk-check] Detected client version: js-sdk@1.4.2 — this version does respect Retry-After but will still retry up to 4 times by default.
maria: ok forwarded the concise guidance + config snippet. keeping this thread for notes — we should add a small entry to support KB about "Avoiding duplicate creates when SDK retries". :+1:
